title: Earthquakes and volcanoes
text: Collect data, map, and describe patterns in the locations of volcanoes and earthquakes related to tectonic plate boundaries, interactions, and hotspots in order to forecast the locations and likelihoods of future events.

items.q: On a world map of the last 10 years of big earthquakes, where do most of the dots fall?
c: Spread evenly across all land and ocean
Mostly in the middle of continents
Mostly in places with hot weather

items.q: Hawaii has active volcanoes but sits far from any plate boundary. What best explains this?
c: A hotspot: hot material rises from deep in the mantle under the plate
Hawaii must secretly be on a plate boundary
Warm ocean water melts the rock
Volcanoes can form anywhere at random

items.q: A town sits right next to a plate boundary where many quakes happened in the past 100 years. What is the best forecast?
c: More quakes are likely there in coming decades
An earthquake will happen there on a date scientists can name
It is safe now because the big quakes already happened
Past quakes tell us nothing about the future

items.q: What can earthquake scientists honestly tell the public today?
c: The chance of a strong quake in an area over a span of years
The exact day and hour of the next big quake
That quakes come after heavy rain
Nothing, because quakes are completely random

items.q: The Ring of Fire around the Pacific Ocean has many volcanoes and earthquakes. Why?
c: Its edges are plate boundaries where plates collide or sink under each other
The Pacific Ocean is warmer than other oceans
The middle of the Pacific Plate is the most active part

items.q: Memphis is near the New Madrid Seismic Zone, which had large quakes in 1811-1812. What should a forecaster conclude?
c: Future quakes are possible there, though rare
No quake can happen there because it is not on a plate boundary
The next quake there will happen in a year scientists already know
Because 200 years passed, the risk is now zero

items.q: On the map, Chile (on a plate boundary) has many big quakes and Brazil (not on a plate boundary) has almost none. What pattern does this show?
A world map of all earthquakes shows a line of dots running down the middle of the Atlantic Ocean. What does that line most likely mark?
c: A plate boundary under the ocean

items.q: A map shows a chain of volcanoes in the middle of the Pacific Plate, getting older toward the northwest. What made them?
c: The plate moving over a hotspot

items.q: Region A had 40 quakes in 10 years. Region B had 2. Which forecast fits the data best?
c: Region A is more likely to have quakes in the coming years
Region B is due for a quake on a known date
Region A is safe now that it had so many
Both regions have the same chance

misconceptions.random: It's easy to think quakes can happen anywhere, but most happen in long belts along plate boundaries.
misconceptions.exact: No one can predict the exact day of a quake. Scientists forecast the chance of one over many years.
misconceptions.hotspot: Not every volcano is at a plate boundary. Some, like Hawaii's, form over a hotspot deep in the mantle.
misconceptions.weather: Weather doesn't cause quakes or volcanoes. They come from plates moving deep underground.
misconceptions.center: Plates are most active at their boundaries, where they meet, not in their middles.
misconceptions.intraplate: Most quakes happen at plate boundaries, but some, like New Madrid near Memphis, happen far from any plate boundary.
misconceptions.once: A big quake doesn't make a place safe. Places with many past quakes are likely to have more.
